hook: A 2-minute self-check could be the reason you catch something early.
caption:
Oral cancer is one of the more detectable cancers when you know what you're looking for, and most people never look. A quick self-exam takes about two minutes and doesn't require any equipment.

Here's what to do: stand in front of a mirror with good light and take a slow look around your mouth. Run your tongue along the roof of your mouth, the insides of your cheeks, and under your tongue. Feel along your jaw and the sides of your neck for anything that feels like a lump or a swollen area.

What you're watching for: white or red patches that weren't there before, a sore that hasn't healed after two weeks, any lump or thickening in your cheek, or a nagging feeling of something stuck when you swallow. Most of the time you won't find anything, and that's the point. But if something looks off, you'll know to follow up.

Once a month is a reasonable habit. It costs nothing and takes less time than brushing your teeth.

Not sure what your risk level looks like? Take the free screener at oralcheck.org.
